questions.q: Name three supporting characters in "HkfDru" and state one specific action or dialogue of each that reveals HkfDru's character.
questions.a: Correct answer: (1) Narrator — observes HkfDru's refusal to reveal her real name, showing HkfDru's fierce self-respect; (2) Chachi (HkfDru's sister) — drags HkfDru by hair when she tries to leave, revealing HkfDru's trapped vulnerability; (3) Narrator's brother (Lakal) — addresses HkfDru as "th" and demands service, exposing caste-based entitlement. A wrong answer lists characters without textual evidence or confuses protagonist traits with supporting character actions, showing the student cannot distinguish between *describing* a character and *using textual evidence to analyze function*.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the narrator's father (फरक) giving HkfDru the name "HkfDru" is symbolically significant, and how this differs from HkfDru's own attitude toward her name.
questions.a: Correct answer: The father imposes the name "HkfDru" (meaning 'one who bears the burden') as an act of ownership, reducing her identity to her labor function. HkfDru never reveals her real name, guarding her inner self from institutional erasure. The contrast shows power dynamics: naming as domination vs. silence as resistance. A wrong answer treats the name as merely descriptive or misses the power imbalance, revealing the student reads literally rather than symbolically — a critical gap for board "explain the significance" questions.

questions.q: In the episode where the narrator's brother (लक्ल) visits and HkfDru serves him, identify two specific textual details that show caste hierarchy operating through language and gesture. Explain the effect of each detail.
questions.a: Correct answer: (1) Lakal addresses HkfDru as "th" (तुम) while the narrator uses "aap" (आप) — linguistic marker of caste superiority; (2) Lakal sits with legs stretched out, expecting service without gratitude — bodily entitlement. Effect: The text shows caste not as abstract idea but as daily performance. A wrong answer generalizes "he was rude" without quoting the pronoun or describing the posture, missing the textual precision board exams demand for "give evidence from the text" questions.

questions.q: Compare how Chachi (चाची) and the narrator's mother (फोएरक) respond to HkfDru's suffering. What does this comparison reveal about women's complicity in patriarchal structures across class lines?
questions.a: Correct answer: Chachi physically abuses HkfDru (dragging by hair, burning with hot tongs) to enforce domestic servitude; the narrator's mother, though gentle, never intervenes structurally — she offers momentary kindness (food, cloth) but accepts the system. Comparison reveals: upper-class women (mother) sustain patriarchy through passive beneficence; lower-class women (Chachi) enforce it through violence because their survival depends on it. A wrong answer treats both as simply "good" or "bad" without analyzing structural position, showing inability to do comparative character analysis — a frequent board competency question type.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "The narrator in 'HkfDru' is a reliable witness to HkfDru's life." Support your judgment with two pieces of textual evidence.
questions.a: Correct answer: The narrator is partially reliable — she documents HkfDru's labor, speech, and resistance with empathy and detail (evidence: recording HkfDru's cooking skills, her refusal to give her name, her grief at her son's death). But she is also complicit: she benefits from HkfDru's labor, never challenges the caste wage gap, and frames HkfDru's story as "beautiful" (सुंदर) — aestheticizing suffering. A wrong answer says "yes, she's the author" or "no, she's biased" without nuance, missing the evaluative skill boards test in "critically examine" questions.

questions.q: Write a 60-word diary entry from the perspective of HkfDru's son (शिशु) on the day he realizes his mother will never leave Chachi's house. Use one metaphor from the text.
questions.a: Expected criteria: First-person voice showing child's limited understanding but emotional clarity; references the "burning tongs" (गर्म चिमटा) or "locked door" metaphor; conveys helplessness without adult vocabulary. Good answer: "आज माँ ने फिर चिमटा नहीं पकड़ा। दरवाज़ा बंद था। मैं रोया नहीं — आँसू सूख जाते हैं जैसे चूल्हे की राख। माँ नहीं आएगी।" A poor answer writes in adult voice, uses no textual metaphor, or exceeds word limit, showing inability to adopt perspective — a creative writing skill tested in board "imaginative response" questions.
